title: How many notes to play the blues
summary: Dick and Albert agree too many notes lose the blues, though Billy Douglas, Punch Miller and Buddy Petit made every note count.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: But there's something slippery about some guys, especially, well, let's say, from the East. The guys from the East to me, you know, they sound like ragtime players of the, with a, uh, I'm talking about piano ragtime, you know, with a lot of notes. A lot of notes. Yeah. And a lot, to me, a lot of wasted notes. Right. And, uh, you don't, it doesn't take many notes to play the blues. If you play too many notes and you don't get the feeling.

Then you're literally from the blues. The blues is just a soulful song that has a simple meaning. Yeah. And when you go to adding this and adding that, then you, you, you deviate from the blues and become something else.
Many great musicians played many notes, but every note counted. Right.

You know. Well, that's what I, I referred to, Billy Douglas, uh, Punch Miller. Mm-hmm. And Buddy Petit, they made a lot of notes. But they made them count. That's right. They put them in the right places and they, they, they added, uh, something to what they were playing. Yeah.
